title: FlowECG: Using Flow Matching to Create a More Efficient ECG Signal Generator
task_model: Diagnosis-conditioned S4 flow matching, retaining SSSD-ECG architecture; 71 binary diagnostic conditions (pp. 2–5, §§2.1,3.1–3.2).
data_protocol: PTB-XL: 21,799 recordings/18,869 patients; 10 s, 1,000 samples, 8 independently generated leads expanded to 12. Hold-out test stated, but fold numbers, split sizes and explicit patient separation unclear; normalization not reported (pp. 2,4).
metrics: DTW (Eq.3), feature-based 1-Wasserstein (Eq.4), spectral similarity 1/(1+mean PSD Wasserstein) (Eq.5), biased empirical squared MMD (Eqs.6–7), and neural function evaluations/NFE. Lead-average aggregation is stated, but Wasserstein also concatenates channel features; exact feature list, kernel/bandwidth, and DTW pairing are unclear (§2.3). Errors lower, spectral similarity higher; units depend on preprocessing. NFE is a computation proxy, not wall-clock latency.
training_losses: Velocity regression E||f_theta(x_t,c,t)−(x_1−x_0)||², x_t a linear interpolation of independent Gaussian noise and ECG; unit coefficient; uniform time sampling; generator network only. Adam 2e−4, batch 6; Euler inference (Eq.8, pp.4–5).
ablation_results: Matched-backbone comparison and NFE sweep, not an isolated regularizer ablation. Table 1 reports MMD 80.70→21.09 and DTW 73.49→83.96 at 200 NFE; lower DTW is better, so it worsens. Claims of improvement on three metrics conflict with prose acknowledging spectral worsening; retain table-specific comparisons, not the headline. 10–25 NFE performance is claimed from Fig.2 (§3.3).
utility_expert_privacy: No downstream classification experiment, blinded clinical panel, or empirical privacy attack reported. Privacy is motivation, not a demonstrated guarantee (whole main text).
reproducibility: Architecture and optimizer specified; uncertainty, repeated seeds and full metric implementation details not reported. Publication footnote says preprint not peer reviewed and proceedings version forthcoming (p.1); do not treat this as confirmed publication.
critical_notes: Reviewer assessment: useful efficiency evidence, but NFE must be paired with time/hardware measurements; feature distributions and unpaired DTW cannot independently establish physiological validity.

title: High-Fidelity Synthetic ECG Generation via Mel-Spectrogram Informed Diffusion Training
task_model: SSSD-ECG with multiresolution mel-spectrogram supervision; diagnostic/form/rhythm groups and age/sex embeddings condition 12-lead generation (§3).
data_protocol: PTB-XL 21,837 records/18,885 patients; 10 s at 100 Hz; explicitly patient-level 17,441/2,193/2,203 train/validation/test (§4). Age bins [12,17,34,54,74], sex 2 classes (§3.2). Additional normalization detail not reported in inspected methods.
metrics: RMSE, MSE, SNR dB, Fourier distance, Hausdorff distance, SSIM; membership inference risk/MIR and nearest-neighbor adversarial accuracy/NNAA; mean/max absolute Pearson interlead correlation error; downstream AUROC with 95% CIs; qualitative outlier clinical-feature distributions (Tables1–4, Appendix A). Pairing/normalization and exact MIR/NNAA implementations are insufficiently specified. Paper marks MIR/NNAA lower as better; NNAA can be negative and is not simply classifier accuracy.
training_losses: L_total=L_MSE+beta L_MIDT (Eq.1): multiresolution mel-magnitude L1 discrepancy between true and reconstructed ECG. Narrative calls MSE both denoising and signal-pointwise error; exact target is ambiguous. Beta, STFT window sizes, hop sizes and mel-bin count not reported; do not invent them (§3.1).
ablation_results: Table2 average correlation error 0.140→0.042 (70% reduction, not abstract's 74%). Table4 synthetic-only AUROC 0.541±0.074→0.640±0.094; with 1 real fold MIDT 0.902±0.004 versus real-only 0.901±0.009. Large-real-data augmentation gains are small (Table3). Reported CIs and p<0.05 annotations lack clear run/test specification in these sections. Table1 MIR for MIDT 0.0081 exceeds gender variant 0.0036, contradicting prose calling MIDT lowest. Discussion makes further ablation/privacy-training claims without matching clearly specified training terms or tables (§5).
utility_expert_privacy: 8 synthetic folds plus increasing real folds, and 8 real folds plus 1–8 synthetic folds (Tables3–4). No formal blinded cardiologist experiment reported; visual examples are not a Turing test. MIR/NNAA are empirical proxies, not differential-privacy guarantees.
reproducibility: Analyzed arXiv v2. Missing loss coefficient and spectral settings prevent exact paper-only reproduction. Demographic conditioning and loss changes require separate ablation; no code inspected.
critical_notes: Reviewer assessment: evidence supports testing spectral supervision, but internal numerical/narrative inconsistencies and underdefined privacy metrics weaken strong trustworthiness claims.

title: Conditional Electrocardiogram Generation Using Hierarchical Variational Autoencoders
task_model: Conditional hierarchical Nouveau VAE adapted to 1D ECG; mixtures of logistic distributions and dependent channels; generate 8 leads then derive 12 (§III).
data_protocol: PTB-XL 21,837; Georgia 10,344; Ningbo 34,905 records. 12 leads, 500 Hz, standardized to 10 s; per-lead 2.5–97.5 percentile filtering; random train/validation/test splits, explicit patient grouping unclear (§IV.B).
metrics: Downstream per-class AUROC (%) averaged over training-data fractions; visual waveform/nearest-real comparisons; matched GPU training budget 134 h on A100. No distributional FID/MMD evaluation reported in own experiments (§§IV–V, TablesVI–VII, Figs2–6).
training_losses: Hierarchical VAE training is described through NVAE architecture and mixture likelihood, but an explicit complete ECG objective and KL coefficients/schedule are not reported. TableV lists 5-epoch warmup and zero normalizing flows; this is not enough to infer KL annealing. Comparator WaveGAN/Pulse2Pulse GP weight=10 (TablesII–III).
ablation_results: Ablates 1D versus 2D architecture and augmentation strategy, not ELBO components. MI-only augmentation gain up to 1.8 percentage points AUROC; both-class gain up to 1.5 (§V.A). Rare-class transfer sometimes worsens versus real-only pretraining (TablesVI–VII). CIs/seeds not reported.
utility_expert_privacy: Fixed real validation/test, synthetic proportions 0.1–1,1.5,2 for whole-data enrichment; 0.1–1 for minority enrichment; class-balanced synthetic pretraining and Georgia/Ningbo fine-tuning (§IV.A). No clinician or attack experiment; clinician validation is future work (§VI).
reproducibility: https://github.com/univanxx/cNVAE_ECG (p.1), not inspected. Batch size 64 in prose versus 32 TableV; equations for limb leads contain a suspected typographical error. Preserve these discrepancies rather than silently correcting the paper.
critical_notes: Reviewer assessment: useful external transfer design, but adaptation on external data is not zero-shot external validation; split ambiguity and absent loss specification limit attribution.

title: SSSD-ECG-nle: New Label Embeddings with Structured State-Space Models for ECG generation
task_model: Conditional SSSD diffusion with separate present/absent label embeddings and a 1×1 folding convolution (§IV.B–C).
data_protocol: PTB-XL 21,837, 10 s, 100 Hz, eight independent leads expanded to 12; retains amplitude, reports bandpass preprocessing. Folds1–8 train,9 validation,10 test; patient grouping follows dataset folds but not independently audited (§IV.A,E).
metrics: TSTR/TRTS G-mean sqrt(sensitivity×specificity), F1, multilabel ROC-AUC; expert diagnostic accuracy and real/fake confusion matrix; convergence versus processed samples. Relation metrics and TSTS explicitly rejected as uninformative (§IV.D–V). Distinguish classification F1 from manifold F1.
training_losses: Inherited diffusion denoising/noise objective described in diffusion background (§III); no new loss term. SSSD settings inherited; exact ECG-specific weighting not separately supplied. New contribution is conditioning, not a changed training loss.
ablation_results: TableI PVC TSTR F1 0.338→0.561; AFIB F1 0.720→0.709 despite broader improvement language. TableII multilabel TSTR AUROC0.820, TRTS0.894. TableIII includes duplicated-positive baseline. Checkpoint study shows disease-dependent convergence and possible undertraining (TableIV).
utility_expert_privacy: 200 ECGs (100 real/100 synthetic) for diagnostic reporting; 20 each of five categories. Separate 380-example detection test: 100 real/280 synthetic; confusion matrix 99,1,1,279 means 378/380 correct (99.47%). Text inconsistently calls 280 records additional to 100 synthetic; table denominator retained. Third physician for detection; years of experience/blinding details not reported (§V.B, TablesV–VI). No privacy attack.
reproducibility: Reports difficulty reproducing original SSSD multilabel TSTR. Generated data/expert results promised; no code inspection. Seed uncertainty not reported.
critical_notes: Reviewer assessment: unusually direct evidence that reasonable downstream utility can coexist with obvious synthetic appearance. Real/fake detectability is not a privacy metric, despite the authors' privacy framing.

title: DiffuSETS: 12-Lead ECG generation conditioned on clinical text reports and patient-specific information
task_model: Text- and patient-conditioned latent diffusion: separately trained VAE plus cross-attention U-Net; age, sex, heart rate and LLM clinical-report embeddings (Methods, Model architecture).
data_protocol: MIMIC-IV-ECG 800,035→794,372 retained recordings; 12 leads, 10 s,500 Hz downsampled to1,024 points (effective102.4 Hz). Excludes missing demographics/undetectable HR; XQRS replaces abnormal RR values. PTB-XL21,799 external records processed identically (Methods, Datasets). Explicit generator patient-level separation unclear in these methods; downstream50,000/task split80/10/10.
metrics: Net1D feature FID (Gaussian feature moment distance; Eq.12), k=3 manifold precision/recall/F1 (Eqs.13–16), conditional HR MAE bpm (Eq.17), paired text–ECG embedding cosine/CLIP score (Eq.18). No raw pointwise MAE for unpaired waveforms. FeatureDB average-wave evaluation in TableS1; detailed supplementary implementation pending. Net1D/contrastive encoder training corpus and independence insufficiently specified in main paper. Diagnosis classifier outcomes and cardiologist real/fake judgments plus text-condition correctness (Results).
training_losses: VAE MSE reconstruction+lambda KL(q(z|x)||N(0,I)); lambda linearly annealed from0, terminal value not specified (Eqs.7–8). Latent diffusion noise prediction MSE (Methods, Eq.5). VAE pretrained separately; T=1000, beta schedule0.00085–0.012, latent4×128; optimizer LR5e−4,batch512 (Implementation details). KL expression printed with log sigma rather than an unambiguously conventional variance notation; use faithful distributional Eq.7.
ablation_results: Table1 internal FID23.6, manifoldF1 .894, HRMAE4.15, CLIP .812. Without patient information HRMAE12.25; without VAE FID48.9. These are component/conditioning ablations, not isolated KL-weight ablations. External PTB-XL FID27.6/HRMAE6.73. No claim of cross-paper ranking.
utility_expert_privacy: Minority augmentation versus real-only and weighted-CE baselines for normality,AF,PVC; 50,000 selected records/task,80/10/10. Two cardiologists evaluate50 generated+50 real ECGs;100 generated reports assessed for semantic correctness (76%). Expertise years, agreement and uncertainty not fully specified (Results, Turing test; Fig.3). No membership attack or formal privacy guarantee.
reproducibility: Published full text analyzed, linked arXiv v1 retained as earlier version. https://github.com/PKUDigitalHealth/DiffuSETS and https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.15331141; no code inspection. Supplement-specific metrics remain explicitly incomplete until supplement retrieval.
critical_notes: Reviewer assessment: broad evaluation spanning distribution, coverage, conditions and experts; encoder dependence, split independence and privacy claims require stronger checks.

title: Introducing a Comprehensive Framework for Synthetic ECG Validation
venue: IEEE open journal of engineering in medicine and biology
task_model: Pulse2Pulse-style WGAN-GP generation of Brugada typeI ECG; six-level U-Net generator, convolutional critic (§II.C).
data_protocol: 21 patients,95.2%male,53±14y; 15s–5min16-lead acquisitions at1kHz,100Hz Chebyshev lowpass/50Hz notch, downsample500Hz;10s windows50%overlap yield1,122 ECGs. Generate1,122 eight-lead records expanded to12; no independent held-out patient evaluation (§II.A–C).
metrics: Visual median-beat/IQR overlays; RR,PR,QRS,QTc and P/QRS/T axes; Mann–Whitney tests with real features aggregated per patient. ED, maximum absolute error (paper's MAE, NOT mean), cosine distance, MSE,RMSE,NMSE,RMSPE, kernel MMD,KL,DTW; FID listed but explicitly NOT used. Real–fake median distances contextualized by real intra-/interpatient distances (§II.D–E,TableII). Metric equations in supplement, not main text. Expert accuracy,sensitivity,specificity,PPV,NPV,F1 (TableIII).
training_losses: WGAN-GP named; paper calls it gradient clipping, although GP and clipping differ. Weight not given in main text; original hyperparameters inherited. Adam1e−4,batch32,2000epochs (§II.C). No loss ablation.
ablation_results: Morphology p>.05 across7 features is non-rejection, not demonstrated equivalence. Expert accuracy50.6%, sensitivity62.3%,specificity39%,F1=55.04% (TablesII–III). n_real=21 patient medians vs n_synthetic=1122; dependence among synthetic records from same trained generator is unaccounted for.
utility_expert_privacy: One cardiologist >5y experience,2244 balanced real/synthetic cases, blinded to prevalence (§II.E). No downstream classifier experiment; independent Brugada data proposed as future work. Linked seven-reader report Zanchi_2025_Brugada is not an independent cohort. Pairwise-distance checks are not membership inference.
reproducibility: Framework and supplementary appendix are described; training and synthetic resources claimed, not executed. Dataset size and sample units distinguish21 people from1122 overlapping windows.
critical_notes: Reviewer assessment: strong practical use of real–real reference distances and patient aggregation. Failure to reject a difference cannot establish equivalence or no memorization; held-out patients and explicit equivalence bounds are needed.

title: f-GAN: A frequency-domain-constrained generative adversarial network for PPG to ECG synthesis
task_model: PPG-conditioned attention-gated U-Net GAN for paired ECG waveform synthesis (§2.2–2.3).
data_protocol: 15 participants,9/3/3 disjoint train/validation/test subjects;40,675/11,276/12,796 training-length segments. Resample128Hz,4s windows with2s overlap; PPG0.4–8Hz,ECG3–45Hz filters,minmax[−1,1]. Evaluate10s windows with8s overlap (§2.1,2.5); external cohort not reported.
metrics: HR MAPE%=100/N sum|HRreal−HRgen|/HRreal; standard peak detector and count of HR extraction failures. Validation mean/SD across31 seeds; best-validation-seed testMAPE; active/inactive strata; visual ECG morphology (§2.5,§3,Eq.4).
training_losses: Original logistic adversarial minimax+0.1×paired L1 FFT-amplitude difference excluding DC. Generator minimizes both, discriminator maximizes adversarial term (Eqs.1–3). Time-domain paired loss deliberately avoided for PPG–ECG latency. Generator/discriminator LR1e−4/1e−5; updates5:1; baseline15epochs vs spectral11epochs (§2.4).
ablation_results: 31 seeds each arm: validation MAPE SD12%→3%; t(60)=3.04,p=.005; failure counts t(60)=2.97,p=.006. Best-seed testMAPE14%→12%, PPG detector15% (Figs3–5,Table1). Different epoch schedules are a residual confound.
utility_expert_privacy: HR extraction is utility, not disease diagnosis. No expert, privacy attack or independent external validation reported.
reproducibility: FFT coefficient and exclusions explicit, more seeds than most reviewed studies. Peak-detection failures reported rather than silently omitted. Dataset name verified from p.1 during final check; no source code inspected.
critical_notes: Reviewer assessment: relatively direct evidence for one spectral term, limited to HR and a small healthy/wearable cohort; correct HR does not validate ST/QT morphology.

title: Generating Realistic Multi-Beat ECG Signals
task_model: Hierarchical single-beat diffusion, learned multivariate feature trajectory, then feature-matched concatenation for multiminute ECG (§III).
data_protocol: MIT-BIH Supraventricular:87h/47subjects;normal/abnormal collapse,~100sample R-centered beats;10,000 synthetic beats/class store. Additional MIT-BIH Arrhythmia check AppendixF. Lead selection,sample frequency,patient-separated split and exact sample counts not fully specified in methods.
metrics: Beat-average DTW,curve Fréchet,Euclidean,RMSE,MAE,MSE,PRD; per-timepoint KL,JS,MMD,Wasserstein,KS,mean/variance/skew differences (AppendixTableIV). Feature distributions and correlations for R/P/Q/T intervals/amplitudes (TableII); R-amplitude matching error mV/counts; downstream accuracy,precision,recall,F1,MCC (TablesI,III,V–VII). These averaged-beat errors are not individual unpaired fidelity.
training_losses: Diffusion/feature-generator training objectives inherited or insufficiently specified; no complete weighted training equation. Eq.1 weighted squared feature discrepancy is an inference-time beat-selection cost, NOT a neural training loss. Matching weights not enumerated (§III).
ablation_results: Synthetic feature-based abnormal-class F1 .479 vs BRIDGE .470 and real .778 (TableIII); normal-class .956 vs .222 and real .906. Thus large overall gains do not imply near-real abnormal performance. No CIs or seeds specified. End-to-end comparison limited to5beats due to memory (§IV.E).
utility_expert_privacy: TSTR evaluated with balancedSVM,decision tree,naiveBayes,SVM. No blinded clinical or privacy-attack study. Long examples do not establish validated minute-scale HRV.
reproducibility: Several unspecified choices in feature generator, split and loss; Appendix provides metric values and examples. No implementation inspected.
critical_notes: Reviewer assessment: useful separation of morphology and temporal structure, but preserve rhythm distributions and report reused-beat rates to assess diversity beyond concatenated duration.

title: Complementarity-Preserving Generative Theory for Multimodal ECG Synthesis: A Quantum-Inspired Approach
task_model: Q-CFD-GAN with complex latent coupling and time/frequency/scalogram decoders; includes waveform output (§IV).
data_protocol: Mendeley multimodal ECG source;70/15/15 patient-level split asserted. 0.5–40Hz bandpass,baseline correction,amplitude normalization,1,000sample segments; STFT256 Hann/50%overlap and Morlet scalogram. Sample counts,lead configuration,Hz and cohort details insufficiently specified (§IV.B,§V.A).
metrics: Embedding variance/excess-variance ratio; classifier-output KL plausibility gap Delta; relative reduction rho; mutual-information complementarity retention and gamma; RMS-energy deviation and kappa; P2P amplitude,spectral entropy and joint RMS/P2P plots (Eqs.1–4,15,TableIII,Figs3–6). Encoder/classifier provenance and MI estimator details unclear; dimensionless normalized scores are specific to this paper.
training_losses: Eq.11/Algorithm1: adversarial+lambda1 CFD+lambda2 interference+lambda3 physiology; CFD aligns complementarity plus orthogonality penalty (Eq.9), interference matches energy (Eq.13), physiology penalizes QRS/ST discrepancy (Eq.10). Critic WGAN-GP. Eq.14 instead omits adversarial term and weights: unresolved inconsistency. Lambda values grid-searched but not reported (§V.B).
ablation_results: TableIII variance .033 vs real .031; classifierKL .157 vs MI-GAN .214; complementarity retention .91 vs .56; RMS3.8% vs11.2%. No uncertainty. Loss-removal ablations listed in design but component-specific numerical results not clearly separated in TableIII.
utility_expert_privacy: Classifier plausibility proxy, no reported TSTR or independent cardiologist panel; no empirical privacy validation.
reproducibility: Unspecified dataset size, trained feature models, MI estimation and selected coefficients impede reproduction; preprint analyzed.
critical_notes: Reviewer assessment: proposed signal constraints warrant testing, but stationary loss conditions and classifier agreement do not by themselves establish clinical validity or the claimed mathematical necessity of complex latents.

title: Synthetic ECG signal generation using generative neural networks
task_model: Five normal-beat GANs: classic, DC-DC, BiLSTM-DC, AE/VAE-DC and WGAN (Model designs).
data_protocol: MIT-BIH48 records/47people,360Hz;109,338 segmented beats,90,502 normal;280points resampled256. Generator uses normal beats. Patient-disjoint holdout not established (Dataset and segmentation).
metrics: DTW, curve Fréchet and Euclidean distances, evaluated as all-pairs300×300 means, distance to chosen template, minimum/best beat and thresholded productivity fraction; subjective morphology inspection (Methods1–5,Eqs14–22). Template/threshold choice changes rankings. Classification accuracy,precision,recall,F1/confusion matrices (Tables13–16). No FID: curve Fréchet is different.
training_losses: Hyperparameter subsection states BCE for models,30epochs,batch9; hybrid model adversarial plus weightedL1 reconstruction, coefficient not reported. WGAN naming and blanket BCE statement leave objective ambiguity; do not substitute a presumed Wasserstein implementation.
ablation_results: Productivity72.3% for classicGAN under DTW, whereas expert visual judgment favors BiLSTM/WGAN (Table12,Performance metrics). Artificially imbalanced binary classifier accuracy .54→.97 after augmentation; real-balanced .95 (Tables13–16). No repeated-seed interval; inconsistent test supports across tables.
utility_expert_privacy: Binary normal/LBBB stress test: normal training class reduced to500 versus~6460 LBBB, then restored using synthetic beats;3216 nominal unseen test beats. No documented patient exclusion from generator pool. Expert protocol unspecified; no privacy attack.
reproducibility: Published2025 article analyzed; code/data statements in original. Exact template choice, hybrid weight and test membership require clarification.
critical_notes: Reviewer: minimum-distance scores reward best-case selection and larger sample pools; productivity threshold constructed from generated outputs is not independent clinical acceptance.

title: Variational autoencoder-based neural electrocardiogram synthesis trained by FEM-based heart simulator
task_model: Conditional Gaussian VAE emulator of UT-Heart finite-element simulations, parameter-conditioned12-lead synthesis; qualifies because learned generator is evaluated (Methods,Model).
data_protocol: 2,880 simulated ECG parameter combinations,16cardiac parameters encoded24dimensions;random1728/576/576 train/val/test;500samples/1s beat at500Hz,HRfixed60;ECG/1024 normalization. No real-patient training or external validation (Dataset,Experimental condition). Online publication2023-12-22;2024 issue.
metrics: Paired Q/R/S/T position MAE in samples,convert to seconds /500; manually marked simulator references versus NeuroKit2 generated landmarks. PSNR=10log10(1/MSE) dB after[0,1]normalization. Abnormal landmark detections excluded; P-wave assessment omitted because identical template (Experimental condition,Table2).
training_losses: Maximize conditional ELBO: expected Gaussian decoder log-likelihood minus KL(q(z|x,Y)||N(0,I));unit KL coefficient,encoder and decoder learned jointly (Training). Inference fixes z=0 rather than sampling (Inference).
ablation_results: Grid over4–10layers and latent2–128;largest latent improves PSNR,optimal depth5–7;NeuroKit2 reference Q/S errors7.58/19.15samples dominate landmark evaluation (Results,Table2,Figs3–6). Architecture ablation,not KL ablation.
utility_expert_privacy: Medical specialist supervises ground-truth landmarks,not blinded realism test. No downstream classifier or privacy evaluation; patient separation not applicable to simulated parameter combinations.
reproducibility: Simulator source cited. Annotation exclusion rule contains inconsistent150ms/100samples conversion; preserve rather than correct. Seed/run uncertainty not reported.
critical_notes: Reviewer: excellent example of defensible paired errors, but emulator accuracy against a simulator is not clinical distribution coverage; z=0 results cannot support stochastic diversity.

title: ODE-Constrained Generative Modeling of Cardiac Dynamics for 12-Lead ECG Synthesis
task_model: WaveGAN/WGAN-GP with intra-/interlead ODE residuals;diagnosis/RR-conditioned12lead300sample beats (§§3–5). Analyzed arXivv2 identifies itself as TMLR02/2026;first preprint2024-09-26.
data_protocol: G12EC10,344records/7,871patients;PTB-XL21,799/18,869;500Hz;patient split80%train+validation,20%test before NeuroKit2 R-centered crop/pad300samples. Only recordings with persistent abnormality propagate labels to beats (§5).
metrics: Specificity at validation-selected target sensitivity;AUROC,AUPRC;interlead identity MSE;visual waveform comparisons.5fold paired t-tests and fold variability;fixed real:synthetic1:2,ratio sweep AppendixA (§6,Tables1–4).
training_losses: Generator −E D(G(z))+lambda_EUL[delta L_intra+(1−delta)L_inter],delta=.6. Intra squared residual of finite-difference derivative versus McSharry RHS;inter matches dependent lead derivative to linear combinations of parent RHS (Eqs8–14). Simulator parameters fitted on training beats. Overall lambda_EUL and GP coefficient not established from extracted text; no guessed defaults.
ablation_results: Delta sweep Fig2 supports retaining both terms. G12EC IAVB specificity .82→.85 at sensitivity .94;PTB-XL NSIVCB AUROC .750→.786 (Tables1,3). Fivefold paired tests reported without multiplicity adjustment; test/cross-validation relationship needs clarification.
utility_expert_privacy: Two classifier backbones,real-only and multiple generative baselines. No privacy attack or blinded specialist assessment demonstrated in extracted main sections.
reproducibility: Published-version text via arXiv,explicit patient separation and fixed augmentation ratio. Source equations and coefficient sweep stronger than rationale alone; code not inspected.
critical_notes: Reviewer: ODE priors may suppress unseen pathology; algebraic limb-lead checks are necessary but do not validate precordial spatial physiology.

title: ECGTwin: Personalized ECG Generation Using Controllable Diffusion Model
task_model: Personalized reference-ECG+target-text/demographics latent diffusion;contrastive Individual Base Extractor and AdaX condition injection (§3).
data_protocol: MIMIC794,372 retained records split744,372/50,000 then grouped by subject into6,408,782/399,499 pairs;explicit cross-split patient exclusion unclear in AppendixC. 12leads10s102.4Hz. ExternalPTB-XL4,269pairs,no fine-tuning (AppendicesC–D).
metrics: Inherited Net1D-based FID/manifoldprecision,recall,F1,HRMAE,CLIP;intra-minus-interpatient cosine similarity Eq9,silhouette,t-SNE;personalized diagnosis metrics and inference steps/s. Quality tests5repeats mean±SD (Table1,AppendixD). Same extractor trains and evaluates identity consistency.
training_losses: Stage1 symmetric contrastive cosine loss with learnabletemperature,positive same-patient pairs (Eq1; denominator printed j≠i);stage2 DDPMnoiseMSE (Eq8). Frozen pretrainedDiffuSETSVAE;no new reconstructionloss. Reference condition and base-vector dropout.15;batch65536 via accumulation for extractor (AppendixC).
ablation_results: Table1 DiT FID26±2.8,F1 .884±.002,HRMAE7.03±.50. External HRMAE10.23 worse than two ablations6.88/7.35 despite bestFID41;tradeoff matters (Table6). Component ablations isolate conditioning architecture,not denoising objective.
utility_expert_privacy: 293held-out evaluation patients;earliestECG reference,synthetic normal/abnormal twins fine-tune patient classifiers,remainingtest records train population model (§4.4). No empirical privacy test; preserving identity raises distinct disclosure questions.
reproducibility: https://github.com/Raiiyf/ECGTwin;not inspected. Preprint analyzed;CIKM2026 program lists acceptance,publication date not independently established.
critical_notes: Reviewer: personalize evaluation with an independent identity model and verify generator/VAE patient overlap;pair counts are not independent patient counts.

title: Simulator and Experience Enhanced Diffusion Model for Comprehensive ECG Generation
task_model: Text/EHR-conditioned latent diffusion with frozenVAE/beatdecoder,simulatorEuler and interlead constraints (§3).
data_protocol: MIMIC-IV-ECG800,03510s12lead500Hz records linked to clinical EHR;4×128latents;XQRS whenHRmissing. Final split sizes,patient separation and retrieval-index restrictions unclear (§4).
metrics: Conditional rawMAE,NRMSE,Pearson;HRMAE;relativeCLIP=generated/real paired-text cosine;relativeFID=synthetic-realFID/real-realFID (Eq26);classificationF1,accuracy,AUROC (Tables1–2). RelativeFID formula should decrease, but table labels upward: unresolved discrepancy.
training_losses: VAE fullMSE+beta_KL KL+beatMSE+alpha_spec averaged squared log-rFFT discrepancy over allbeats (Eqs12–16). Diffusion noiseMSE+lambda Euler+gamma interlead (Eqs17–23);globalcoefficients not specified. Simulatorfitting adds affine/trendMSE,scale,width,amplitude and phase-order penalties (AppendixA.3).
ablation_results: Table1 noSim HRMAE14.28 versusfull8.43;noInterLead19.21. Critical equation ambiguity: regularizers described on h=Dbeat(z0) with frozen encoder/decoder,not predicted z0;as written no denoiser gradient path. Code inspection needed before assuming implemented regularization matches paper. No CI/test statistics in comparison tables.
utility_expert_privacy: Minoritysex andSVT augmentation versus skewed/balancedreal andDiffuSETS;SVTAUROC .80→.85,balancedreference .93 (Table2). No blindedclinician or privacy attacks reported.
reproducibility: Preprint;weights and gradient-path ambiguity are material. Same-label waveform pairing does not imply temporal groundtruth alignment.
critical_notes: Reviewer: promising hybrid objective, but cannot recommend exact reproduction without resolving gradient dependence and relativeFID direction.

title: Synthetic ECG Generation for Data Augmentation and Transfer Learning in Arrhythmia Classification
task_model: Comparison of SSSD/Diffwave,conditionalUnet1D(Time-Diffusion),and Time-VQVAE with bidirectional masked-tokenpriors (§5).
data_protocol: PTB-XL andChapman,12lead10s,seven commonrhythm classes. Dataset descriptive counts18,885 and45,152patients;per-class selectedcountsTable4. Hz/split patientgrouping not fully resolved from methods;do not infer from originaldataset (§4,§8).
metrics: t-SNE,UMAP,PaCMAP;RBF-MMD;two-sample real/fakeclassifier accuracy50%target;classificationaccuracy,precision,recall,F1,ROC-AUC;25repeataverages (§7–8).
training_losses: Diffusion variational/noisedenoising objectives inherited;Time-VQVAE separatesLF/HF STFT quantization thenmasked-tokenpriortraining. Complete weightedobjectives/codeconfigs not specified in paper (§5);classificationloss separate from generatorloss.
ablation_results: Single-datasetaugmentation benefit limited;mergingdatasets improves results;syntheticpretraining alone remains weaker thanreal-only (Results,Conclusion).25repeats improve repeatability but do not fix patientleakage.
utility_expert_privacy: TRTR,TSTS,TSTR,TRTS,mixedtrain/realtest;fine-tunes classifierhead on20/40/60/80%realdata withfeaturelayersfrozen (§7–8). No expert/privacyattackstudy.
reproducibility: Selects openimplementations thattrain without major tuning;reproducibility selection limits completeness of modelcomparison. Preprint analyzed.
critical_notes: Reviewer: negativefindings and real-only reference are valuable;TSTS and embeddings cannot replace held-outrealutility.

title: Data imbalance in cardiac health diagnostics using CECG-GAN
task_model: TransformerconditionalGAN with encoder/decoder latentmapping for minoritybeataugmentation (Methods).
data_protocol: MIT-BIH47subjects,300point R-centeredbeats;db5nine-levelwaveletdenoising;N/A/V/L/R. CSPC2020additional10patients,~24h each. ResNettrainrate.8;independentpatienttest and generator/classifier split boundaries unclear (Methods,Tables3,9–11).
metrics: PRD,curveFD,RMSE,MAE;classificationprecision,recall,F1;denoisingSNR is preprocessingassessment,not generativefidelity. FD formula underdefined. Sample-selection accepts generateddata when classifierperformance improves (Table4,selectionsection).
training_losses: Encoder/decoderreconstruction,latentgeneratoralignment,and conditionaladversarialtraining described as stages;complete equations and coefficients not reported in methods. No directlossablation (Table4).
ablation_results: MIT-BIH averageF1 94.102→98.7255%;minorityA1950→68024examples;CSPCresults also improve (Tables9–11). No independenttest restriction on classifier-driven sampleselection stated;potentialselectionleakage.
utility_expert_privacy: Augmentation experiments,not TSTR. No blindedexpert or privacyattack. Synthesizing from3–4people per grouplimits diversity (Discussion).
reproducibility: Normalization/pairing and exactobjective incomplete. Reported externaldataset is retrainingevaluation,not verifiedzero-shotvalidation.
critical_notes: Reviewer: benefits cannot be attributed to a specific loss;validate selection onvalidationdata only and keep realtest untouched.

title: Minority class-aware multiclass arrhythmia detection using conditional GAN augmentation
task_model: Class-conditional WGAN-GP generates minority PhysioNet2020 ECG classes for eight-class diagnosis augmentation (Methods §§2–4).
data_protocol: PhysioNet2020, eight classes,360Hz single lead,360 samples. Each class360 synthetic examples; fivefold CV reported but patient partition details absent.
metrics: Classifier accuracy/precision/recall/F1, DTW and SSIM waveform similarity; definitions and real/synthetic pair protocol unclear (Results tables3–4).
training_losses: cWGAN-GP critic objective includes gradient penalty coefficient10; Eq.1 sign places GP under critic maximization, inconsistent with conventional minimization description. Auxiliary class loss weight unspecified. Diffusion not used.
ablation_results: Noaug macro F1 .78; GAN +ResNet .89; full .94 (Table3). Table4 fivefold scores .932,.945,.938,.941,.944 incompatible with printed SD .012 under common sample SD.
utility_expert_privacy: Only TSTR-like classifier augmentation assessment, class balance and grouped patient split unclear; no expert or attack.
reproducibility: Full XML; equations and tables have material inconsistencies; code not inspected.
critical_notes: Potential record-level leakage with 360Hz chopped segments. DTW/SSIM do not establish diagnostic validity; Table variance is internally inconsistent.

title: Single-Lead ECG Arrhythmia Classification Based on Peak-Enhanced Attention Network and Quality-Aware GAN Data Augmentation Framework
task_model: Quality-aware GAN augmentation learns soft labels from ECG quality/rhythm signals, generates 12-lead records, evaluates classifier and waveform quality.
data_protocol: PhysioNet2017-derived 8,528 records, remove46 poor quality, 80/20 record split then 10-s windows; no patient-level separation specified. AF examples expanded1841→6000.
metrics: Classifier accuracy/F1, Kurtosis excess K=E4/var², ECG quality diagnostics; classifier parameter/FLOPs and inference latency refer downstream classifier rather than GAN (Methods/Table10–11).
training_losses: Soft quality targets alpha=.7; generator/discriminator adversarial objective (Eq.10); positive-label loss is −E[y logD] only, not full soft-label BCE. Eq.11 specificity denominator malformed (includes TN twice).
ablation_results: GAN ablation F1 .816 vs noaug .793; full system .880 includes classifier architecture changes, not attributable solely to waveform fidelity (Table10–11).
utility_expert_privacy: Augmentation classification benefit only; no blinded reviewers or privacy attacks.
reproducibility: Full XML; detailed data and architecture but no patient-stratification protocol or independent test/seed CIs.
critical_notes: High kurtosis may also signal sharp artifacts, so quality weighting requires clinical labels and robustness controls; classifier and generator changes are confounded.

title: UniECG: Understanding and Generating ECG in One Unified Model
task_model: Text-conditioned 12-lead generation through eight special language-model tokens, a learned mapper, and a pretrained DiffuSETS generator; also ECG interpretation, which is a separate endpoint (pp.3–5).
data_protocol: MIMIC-IV-ECG: 737,875 training records after excluding first 50,000 and 2,381 GEM test records; 10,000 generation test records sampled from the first 50,000. Record separation is explicit; patient separation and generator pretraining overlap are not established here. Original DiffuSETS signal preprocessing is inherited (p.5 §4.1).
metrics: Generation Table 2: FID ↓, manifold precision/recall/F1 ↑, HR mean absolute error ↓ (bpm under the inherited protocol), ECG–text CLIP similarity ↑, and decoding success rate ↑. Feature extractor and implementation inherit DiffuSETS rather than being redefined. No paired raw waveform metric. GLM-5 interpretation scores in Table 1 evaluate explanations, not generated ECG clinical validity (pp.4–6).
training_losses: Interpretation token negative log likelihood Eq.3. Generation token NLL Eq.4 with separate start/first/remainder lambda weights (numerical values not reported); mapper squared L2 to frozen DiffuSETS text embeddings Eq.5; total generation L_e+L_d Eq.6, unit top-level weights. Only specified embeddings, head, last eight transformer blocks, normalization, and mapper are updated; underlying waveform generator is pretrained (pp.3–5).
ablation_results: Table 2: FID 79.43 versus direct DiffuSETS 25.26; recall .615 versus .709; HR error 11.72 versus 8.70; success 95.61% versus 100%. No uncertainty or isolated loss ablation reported (pp.5–6).
utility_expert_privacy: No completed medical-student study; human educational evaluation is future work. No membership attack, external generation validation, or TSTR experiment (pp.5–6).
reproducibility: Analyzed arXiv v2 manuscript carries RespMultimodal@KDD 2026 header. Training settings given; generator inherited. Code execution and metric reproduction not performed.
critical_notes: A useful counterexample to treating interface capability as improved waveform quality. Interpretation accuracy cannot substitute for validation of the separately generated teaching cases. Decoding failures should remain in the denominator.

title: PG-LRF: Physiology-Guided Latent Rectified Flow for Electro-Hemodynamic PPG-to-ECG Generation
task_model: PPG-conditioned latent rectified flow with physiology-aware variational autoencoder and fitted electro-hemodynamic simulator; paired waveform generation subgroup (pp.4–7).
data_protocol: MC-MED source: 118,385 visits, 70,545 adults. Synchronized 10-s, one-channel ECG at 120 Hz and PPG at 40 Hz; per-window z-score, invalid windows excluded; official train/test splits used. Actual retained window counts and patient separation details not restated (p.7).
metrics: Paired MAE/RMSE ↓ (normalized units), FD/FID ↓ (distinct names, implementation/extractor insufficiently specified), HR-MAE ↓ bpm; three-run mean±SD. Paired fiducial MAE: PR, QRS, QT, QTcF, P/T duration in ms and ST-J60 in normalized amplitude. Visit-level ICD per-class/macro AUROC ↑; classifier architecture and split held constant (pp.7–9 Tables1–3).
training_losses: PAE Eq.19: lambda_PAT circular phase-delay squared error + dual waveform reconstruction + beta KL to N(0,I) + lambda_GPA mean/symmetric-posterior-KL alignment + lambda_LID bidirectional contrastive loss + lambda_CSD cross-decoding MSE. Flow Eq.26: velocity MSE + lambda_e ECG Euler residual + lambda_p PPG Euler residual; residuals act on differentiably integrated terminal generated waveform, frozen decoder and forward mapper (Eqs.21–26). Main training coefficients/contrastive temperature not reported numerically in inspected methods. Separate simulator-fitting objective Eq.36 uses ECG 5, PPG .25, derivative 3, peak-window 12; first half ECG-only warmup; top-100 training ICD groups (Appendix B pp.14–15).
ablation_results: Removing simulator guidance worsens HR-MAE 3.94±.76 to 4.94±.57 and FID 37.79±.27 to 45.90±.27; separate-autoencoder ablation HR 6.36±.07. Three runs; no uncertainty for external cohorts (Table1).
utility_expert_privacy: Macro-AUROC .633±.01 versus PPG .545±.04. Authors explicitly caution that visit ICD labels are not ECG-only diagnoses (pp.8–9). No blinded experts, privacy attacks, or external dataset experiment reported.
reproducibility: Preprint; equations and simulator-fitting weights available. Main loss weights, exact metric feature model, retained counts and fiducial failure policy remain insufficient for independent reproduction.
critical_notes: Physiology guidance improves measured endpoints within this experiment; it does not establish uniquely recoverable electrical information from PPG. Simulator consistency means proximity to a fitted model, not clinical correctness. Unlike an input-only regularizer, terminal-sample losses here specify a gradient path.

title: Personalized Heart Disease Detection via ECG Digital Twin Generation
task_model: LA VQ-Editor edits a patient’s normal ECG with disease features from a reference patient using vector quantization, ClinicalBERT text guidance and adversarial waveform decoding (pp.3–5).
data_protocol: PTB-XL single-label superclasses; 291 patients with normal and disease records reserved for personalized testing. Remaining patients train/validate. R-peak crop: 100 points before first to 100 after seventh peak, resized to 4096; 12 leads. Training source rate not explicitly restated in inspected methods (p.5).
metrics: ECG-feature Gaussian Fréchet ResNet Distance (FRD) ↓ and ResNet Score (IS analogue) ↑ using training-set pretrained 1D ResNet-101; manifold precision/recall/F1 ↑. Patient/record accuracy, F1, AUROC and ATE difference in group accuracy ↑. DTW to same-patient disease record ↓ for ablations. Privacy attack F1 ↑ means greater risk; feature Euclidean nearest-neighbour threshold epsilon=tau×mean distance. t-SNE qualitative (pp.5–8 Tables1–4).
training_losses: Generator Eq.10: logistic softplus adversarial + L2 reconstruction (Eq.8 written as norm, not explicitly squared) + 1−cosine disease similarity + masked VQ codebook/commitment squared errors, unit coefficients. Discriminator Eq.13: softplus adversarial + disease cosine loss. VQ terms use stop gradients; frozen ClinicalBERT; cross-attention threshold .5 (pp.3–5).
ablation_results: Table3 FRD 1.6286 against real-real .3014, recall .6438 versus CGAN .0688. Ablation Table4 full DTW 5.322×10^3 and ATE 5.13%; component removals worsen these. No multi-seed uncertainty reported.
utility_expert_privacy: For each experimental test patient’s normal ECG, 50 disease variants are added to classifier training; this is explicitly personalized/transductive utility, not ordinary unseen-patient TSTR. Real 15,553 with generated 8,600/17,200/34,400 compared. ATE can rise partly because control-group performance falls (p.6). Privacy feature-distance attack tested across thresholds, no DP guarantee; no independent experts.
reproducibility: Detailed architecture, optimizer and 500-epoch generator training given. Feature extractor trained on training data. Attack calibration, seed uncertainty and complete paired-reference selection need further specification.
critical_notes: Retention of target patient identity and removal of reference identity are different goals. A low single-attack F1 does not prove anonymity. Different acquisition times mean same-patient disease ECGs are not exact paired counterfactual ground truth.

title: PPGFlowECG: Latent Rectified Flow with Cross-Modal Encoding for PPG-Guided ECG Generation and Cardiovascular Disease Detection
task_model: PPGFlowECG: shared variational CardioAlign representation followed by PPG-conditioned latent rectified flow; paired waveform subgroup (pp.3–5).
data_protocol: Lead II, 10-s non-overlapping windows, 128 Hz, z-score. MC-MED official split: 10,356,840/1,299,869/37,052 train/validation/test windows; MIMIC-AFib 35 subjects, 2044/577 train/test; VitalDB 6388 patients, 1,007,165/10,720; BIDMC53, 1458/326. Other datasets split 80/20 by subject (TableII, p.5).
metrics: Paired MAE/RMSE ↓ normalized amplitude and Hamilton-derived HR-MAE ↓ bpm. Per-class/macro AUROC, AF accuracy/F1 ↑. Five cardiologists: real/fake accuracy against chance with 95% CI, and AF accuracy/sensitivity/specificity mean±SD across raters. Grad-CAM and waveform overlays qualitative; no FID or explicit privacy metric in analyzed version (pp.5–8).
training_losses: CardioAlign Eq.6 = global mean plus symmetric Gaussian-KL alignment (Eq.3) + bidirectional contrastive instance loss (Eq.4, temperature not numerically specified) + cross-modal decoding MSE (Eq.5), unit weights. Stage2 squared velocity flow matching E||v−(target−noise)||² Eq.8; frozen encoder/decoder at generation stage; Euler solver (pp.3–4).
ablation_results: Module ablations TableV HR-MAE 3.28 baseline, 1.93 alignment, 2.12 flow, 1.80 full; macro AUROC53.1/61.5/58.9/63.1%. Main10 steps;5 steps slightly better in Fig.5. No isolated ablation for each alignment loss or training-seed intervals (pp.6–7).
utility_expert_privacy: Zero-shot MC-MED→MIMIC-AFib AF F1 .82 versus internal .87. Five board-certified cardiologists (1 junior,3 mid,1 senior), randomized50real/50synthetic real/fake task; one rater accuracy .65. Separate100 balanced AF cases under PPG, PPG+realECG, PPG+syntheticECG: accuracy .81±.13/.89±.07/.87±.09 (p.8 TableVI). No MIA.
reproducibility: Dataset split counts and expert composition unusually explicit; no released-code verification. Blinding across repeated modality conditions, washout, rater agreement and detailed signal-quality exclusion implementation not established.
critical_notes: Expert clinical task is more informative than real/fake discrimination alone, but small sample and repeated cases limit inference. Multiple trained-dataset results are not all external validation; only the stated zero-shot experiment is. Lower MAE does not consistently coincide with best HR error across baselines.

title: Bayesian ECG reconstruction using denoising diffusion generative models
task_model: ECGDiff conditional variance-exploding denoising diffusion for healthy beats; age/sex/RR conditioning, then Bayesian SMC posterior sampling for reconstruction and anomaly detection. Included because unconditional/conditional prior generation is explicitly evaluated (§2.6).
data_protocol: PhysioNet2021: 43,101 records; normal beats from28,167 patients and MI468. Nine channels aVL/aVR/aVF/V1–V6,250Hz,176samples (704ms) around R peak; each lead divided by QRS maximum absolute amplitude. Generation evaluation samples one beat/patient;22580 training patients,2864 test; CV remainder reported separately (pp.4–6).
metrics: Generation: EMD optimal transport on concatenated waveform and conditioning attributes, equal2864-sized real/generated sets, training batches and real-real/noisy-real references; lower. Random-network distillation support-uncertainty: mean squared representation mismatch across10 bootstrap network pairs,1024D,20epochs; lower not automatically better than real reference. Reconstruction R² ↑ and rescaled Mahalanobis distance; QT–RR physiology curves,95%CLT intervals; MI ROC/AUC (pp.6,10–14).
training_losses: Eq.5 weighted clean-signal denoising squared error sum_k gamma_k² E||D(x+sigma_k epsilon,sigma_k)−x||². Preconditioning c_skip/c_out/c_in and sigma_data described §2.5. Exact chosen gamma schedule should be checked against implementation; not inferred from generic diffusion practice. Gaussian observation likelihood and SMC weights are inference operations, not extra neural training losses (§3).
ablation_results: Generation EMD evaluated2–150steps, conditioned versus unconditioned and real-real references (Fig.2). R² missing-precordial-lead .98–.99 versus Dower .71–.87,95%CLT intervals (Table1). MI AUC .75 male/.70 female Fig.10, separate diagnostic task.
utility_expert_privacy: No augmentation/TSTR, blinded experts or privacy attack. Posterior uncertainty and random-network uncertainty have different meanings; neither establishes privacy. Healthy prior deliberately does not preserve pathology in anomaly-detection reconstruction (§3.3.4).
reproducibility: Readable arXiv manuscript; equations and sampling algorithms explicit. Exact trained checkpoint and code not executed; generation metric cost mixes normalized amplitudes and condition scales.
critical_notes: Healthy beats and QRS amplitude normalization restrict claims about arrhythmia, absolute voltages and long-duration HRV. Normalized R² for lead reconstruction cannot be compared to whole-record unconditional generation fidelity. EMD real-real reference is a useful design, but sample count and feature scaling must stay fixed.

title: CoFE: A Framework Generating Counterfactual ECG for Explainable Cardiac AI-Diagnostics
task_model: StyleGAN2 waveform counterfactual framework with learned inversion and fixed diagnostic predictor; explicitly measures generated waveform features (§§2,4).
data_protocol: Generator300,000 MIMIC-IV12-lead ECGs at250Hz; diagnostic models use10s. Evaluation1000 MIMIC ECGs disjoint from potassium predictor training; generator/patient-level separation not established. Paper calls AF classifier training PhysioNet2017 while describing12-lead models: lead harmonization unclear (pp.2–3).
metrics: Before/after P amplitude(mV), RR variability(ms; exact statistic unspecified), T amplitude(mV), QRSduration(ms); p<.05 for each without named test, multiplicity, effect uncertainty or detector details. Saliency maps and prediction changes qualitative (p.4 Table1).
training_losses: Standard logistic minimax GAN objective; frozen-generator encoder reconstruction squared L2. Counterfactual latent-code optimization minimizes target-class cross-entropy through frozen predictor and generator (p.2). This is inference-time optimization, not generator retraining. Regression-target objective for potassium example not specified by the displayed class-CE equation.
ablation_results: P amplitude .09→.04mV, RR variability46.17→85.44ms, T .18→.58mV, QRS95.84→121.98ms (Table1). No isolated loss ablation, synthetic utility comparison, realism coverage score or seed analysis.
utility_expert_privacy: No blinded clinical assessment, membership attack or downstream TSTR. Agreement with classifier-targeted features is not independent diagnosis; fixed predictor is both optimization target and displayed success measure (§§2.2,4).
reproducibility: Demo video supplied; generator checkpoints, training splits, counterfactual stopping criterion and hyperparameters insufficiently specified in5-page report.
critical_notes: Shows how to inspect morphology under counterfactual edits but does not demonstrate causality. Latent optimization alone does not ensure samples remain representative of the original latent prior. Report target success together with edit size and independent clinical review.

title: P2Es: Physiology-Conditioned Diffusion for 12-Lead ECG Generation from PPG
task_model: Conditional diffusion translates PPG to 12-lead ECG. A domain-adjacent waveform synthesis study included because it reports generated waveform evaluation (pp.5–8).
data_protocol: MIMIC II/III/IV after overlap removal; 125 Hz, 2-s windows, subject-wise z-score, patient-level 80/20 split; final merged set count not stated in inspected methods. Ablations and bidirectional III↔IV cross-dataset assessment (pp.7,11–12).
metrics: Paired-reference MSE, multilead DTW, variance of waveform error, KL between selected feature distributions, marginal Wasserstein, and limb-lead electrical-axis cosine similarity (Table 1 p.8). This is translation fidelity. MACs/latency/model size separate; no expert or privacy assessment.
training_losses: Contrastive PPG-to-affinity-group cross entropy Eq.6 (temperature unspecified). Total Eq.18 = lambda1 interlead relation error + lambda2 Fourier-domain L2 + lambda3 axis L2 + lambda4 alignment penalty; coefficients 1,.5,.2,.3. Alignment Eq.17 sums R-peak position, amplitude-range, and heart-rate-count discrepancy. Bespoke frequency-blur/QRS-adaptive corruption is process design, not a separately identified additive training loss (pp.5–7).
ablation_results: MIMIC IV full model Table2 MSE .0902, DTW .0583, error variance .4647, KL .4920, MW 8.0902, axis cosine .9542. Ablations remove affinity, frequency processing, multiscale reverse architecture; full best. 50 DDIM steps, reported 81% faster than 1000-step DDPM (pp.7–12).
utility_expert_privacy: No clear TSTR with independent classifier trained only on generated ECG. Patient-level split and cross-dataset reverse-direction degradation MIMICIII→IV MSE .1056 vs within .0914 (p.12). No clinician/privacy protocol.
reproducibility: Substantial implementation and split detail, 57M+ parameters; code/checkpoint availability not verified. Exact final sample count and some loss scale details unavailable.
critical_notes: Paired errors measure translation with paired targets and aligned windows. Multiple baselines share protocol, but clinical-grade claims exceed the outcomes; authors note single-lead ECG cannot substitute for diagnostic 12-lead ECG.

title: AI modeling photoplethysmography to electrocardiography useful for predicting cardiovascular disease
task_model: CardioPPG translates PPG to ECG with STFT low/high bands, quantized VQ-VAE tokens and PPG-conditioned bidirectional transformers that iteratively reveal masked tokens (npj Digital Medicine 2025; Methods “Conditional generative model with TimeVQVAE”).
data_protocol: Paired 10-s ECG/PPG windows standardized to 256Hz, amplitudes [-1,1], no explicit lag correction. Source 8,942,348 paired segments over 3 sources; PulseDB-MIMIC subset split 70/10/20 by subject for downstream tasks; external ring AF train44/test40 subjects. Generation metric cohort/count details appear supplemental and were unavailable.
metrics: MAE/MSE ↓ paired waveforms, PSNR/SSIM ↑, FID ↓ with ROCKET features, FD ↓ raw first/second moments, MDD marginal density, ACD autocorrelation difference, SD/KD skew/kurtosis differences. 95% bootstrap CIs, 1000 resamples; STFT window n32 vs16/64/128. No expert or privacy attack in main article (“Quality assessment…”).
training_losses: VQ stage STFT32, separate LF/HF encoders/codebooks; summed squared dictionary and beta commitment terms plus LF/HF reconstruction L2; beta unspecified. Frozen quantizer/decoder in stage2. Two masked-token cross entropies: LF tokens conditional on masked LF and PPG; HF conditional on LF, masked HF and PPG; iterative masked inference with cosine schedule. Contrastive pretraining bidirectional CE tau=.05 (Methods).
ablation_results: Text states CardioPPG beats RDDM/WGAN/RecQRS on most metrics; examples FID .001 vs .008 and ACD .367 vs31.046. 1000-bootstrap CIs in supplement. No explicit isolated loss ablation in extracted methods.
utility_expert_privacy: Primary emphasis is CVD screening with subject-level cohorts and external smart-ring PPG AF test. This supports utility for that task, not independently diagnostic waveform validity. No generated ECG clinician blinding/privacy reported. Code URL github.com/Yukui-1999/CardioPPG.
reproducibility: Published full text and code URL available. Detailed CIs and generation cohort are supplemental; supplement not locally available and was not used.
critical_notes: PPG-to-ECG lag is not corrected; paired MAE can penalize phase offsets and cannot be compared with unconditional generation. Feature/distribution scores depend on ROCKET and preprocessing.

title: Deep conditional generative model for personalization of 12-lead electrocardiograms and cardiovascular risk prediction
task_model: Conditional VAE generates subject-specific 12-lead ECG from anatomy/demographics/electrode positions; explicitly generates samples and evaluates morphology against in-silico simulation (Methods §2.5; Results §§3.1–3.2).
data_protocol: UK Biobank 37,508 participants; 10-s,500Hz,12 leads; 21,083 paired ECG/MRI cases for anatomy experiments. Each VAE 80/20 train/test, batch64,80 epochs; split unit called dataset and subject-disjointness unclear. Median beats used in most analyses. Separate incident-CVD cohort 33,713 subjects.
metrics: Morphological trends by lead under heart translation/rotation compared qualitatively with mechanistic simulation; only partial lead-wise agreement and some directional disagreements (§§3.1–3.2). Incident risk C-index .63; +sex/age .65 (§3.3), separate risk model, not generation fidelity. No scalar FID, expert, privacy or TSTR.
training_losses: Conditional ELBO Eq.14: negative expected log-likelihood represented by waveform MSE plus beta KL(q(z|x,y)||N(0,I)); beta example 1e-4. Anatomy condition concatenated into encoder and decoder; random latent samples generate signal (Methods §2.5).
ablation_results: Anatomical rotation/translation trends compared against Mincholé simulation; agreement varies by lead and some trends are opposite (Results §§3.1–3.2). C-index is not a generative quality score. No multi-run uncertainty.
utility_expert_privacy: No held-out generation metric or independent clinicians; no TSTR or MIA. 1,834 electrode-position subset; generative model split protocol underspecified.
reproducibility: Peer-reviewed Frontiers Digital Health full text and architecture available. ELBO and MRI subset count reported; beta setting example only.
critical_notes: Comparison tests anatomy-conditioned trends rather than population distributions. Incomplete and opposite lead trends qualify physiological-consistency claims.

title: A Comprehensive Evaluation Framework for Synthetic ECG: Assessing Fidelity, Utility, and Privacy
task_model: University of Waterloo MSc thesis evaluates conditional SSSD-ECG on PTB-XL using multi-domain fidelity, TSTR/TRTR utility, forecasting, and seven membership attacks (repository first deposit 2026-05-08; thesis §§3–4).
data_protocol: PTB-XL 21,837 records/18,885 patients,12 leads,10s, downsampled 100Hz/1000 samples, per-lead dataset z-score. Official folds1–8 train,9 validation,10 test, multi-hot five superclass labels; diffusion uses 8 independent leads and derives 4 (pp.42–48).
metrics: Utility: ResNet AUROC/F1,1000 bootstrap CIs; lead-aware one-step LSTM RMSE/Pearson. Fidelity: 12-lead ACF MAE, Welch Hann PSD log-MAE, lead-specific FastDTW 20-random-candidate minimum with real-real ratio, db4 level4 normalized wavelet energy MAE, NeuroKit2 LeadII HR/RR/SDNN/RMSSD/QRS count/R amplitude MAPE (pp.49–53). Privacy: seven black/grey-box attacks in Euclidean, DTW, wavelet domains; AUC, TPR@1/10%FPR, DCR/NNDR ratios, global and single-label subgroup (pp.54–58).
training_losses: 200-step conditional DDPM, linear beta 1e-4 to .02; noise-prediction MSE; eight channels,36 bidirectional S4 residual layers, class embedding; Adam 2e-4,2000 epochs,H100 (pp.46–48).
ablation_results: TSTR AUC .828 [.818,.839] vs TRTR .886 [.878,.895]; TSTR F1 .607/.685. ACF MAE .0065, PSD log-MAE .269, LeadI DTW RS/RR ratio1.003. Global MIA AUC .500–.539; DTW .539±.009 over five seeds. Per-class Euclidean-feature HYP AUC .607 on only56 nonmembers (pp.61,63,70,87–90). HRV discrepancies despite strong aggregate ACF/DTW (pp.86,96).
utility_expert_privacy: No clinicians. Global MIA is low, but subgroup HYP attack .607 has a small evaluation group. TSTR remains below real-trained performance, HYP weakest. Forecasting Pearson .918 vs .923; RMSE .1058 vs .1025 (p.63).
reproducibility: Explicit implementation, splits, seeds and attack detail; thesis not peer reviewed. Validate with independent implementation and shadow attacks.
critical_notes: Useful comparison of aggregate similarity with precise HRV and attacks. Single split/checkpoint and PTB-XL constrain generalization; low attack AUC does not establish formal privacy, fairness or attribute protection.

title: Towards High-Fidelity ECG Generation: Evaluation via Quality Metrics and Human Feedback
status: Peer-reviewed conference paper; related thesis version analyzed
task_model: Proceedings version of thesis project evaluates SSSD-ECG fidelity/diversity/utility and clinical feedback. Related December2024 MSc thesis is analyzed as precursor; eligible publication is BIOSTEC2025, DOI10.5220/0013400500003911.
data_protocol: PTB-XL 12 lead. Thesis implementation uses100Hz/10s and official fold split. Questionnaire20 ECG images:10 synthetic,10 real; three reviewers (cardiologist, internist, final-year medical student), July; images test recognition, not diagnosis (thesis §§3–5).
metrics: Improved precision/recall, density, coverage; synthetic training TSTR and related TRTS/TSTS classification. Human real/synthetic ECG recognition and quality tier; CNN ensemble sample-quality class compared to aggregate fidelity. Definitions inherited from metric papers.
training_losses: SSSD-ECG conditional diffusion noise-prediction MSE inherited. Thesis searches S4 layers, label embedding, diffusion steps; not controlled loss comparison. Evaluator five CNNs, class-weighted multiclass CE (thesis pp.34–38).
ablation_results: Thesis: eight of ten synthetic signals misclassified as real by two evaluators with available follow-up; third reviewer follow-up missing. Best hyperparameter evaluator calls96% real and precision .94/density3.85, yet recall .03/coverage .89: fidelity/coverage trade-off (pp.48–49).
utility_expert_privacy: Not an independent blinded cardiology panel; one student, two physicians,20 image-rendered traces and selected outputs. Evaluator uses custom quality data; independence from generator data unclear. No privacy attack.
reproducibility: Public thesis full text deposited2024-12 and 2025 conference paper. Thesis PDF read; proceedings PDF identified but not downloaded. Report only thesis-specific figures as such.
critical_notes: Exploratory support for separate sample realism, distribution fidelity and coverage. Small human sample and correlated custom data limit evaluator validation.

title: CLEP-GAN: An Innovative Approach to Subject-Independent ECG Reconstruction from PPG Signals
task_model: CLEP-GAN and CLEP-VQGAN use contrastive PPG/ECG latent alignment and waveform GAN decoding for PPG-conditioned ECG synthesis (pp.15–18).
data_protocol: BIDMC and CapnoBase paired PPG/ECG;34 pairs/dataset selected,15% random test split, subject-disjointness unclear.512 samples at125Hz (~4s).
metrics: Paired RMSE, FD in feature space, HR MAE, RR interval mean/SD, RR-distribution rHI/rRMSE/rEMD/KL/KS; generator timing/FLOPs and FD efficiency table. Accuracy endpoints on generated traces are not diagnostic validation (pp.18–25).
training_losses: Generation Eq.16: NT-Xent PPG→ECG tau.1 + smooth-L1 PPG autoencoding, ECG autoencoding, crossmodal ECG reconstruction. VQVAE variant adds dictionary/commitment losses lambda=.25 (Eqs.17–18). Time- and STFT-frequency logistic GAN losses, total alpha Lgen+beta Lt+gamma Lf; alpha30,beta3,gamma1 (Eqs.19–21).
ablation_results: Table4: BIDMC RMSE .37 and FD22.27 CLEP-GAN; CapnoBase .33 and FD32.45. Ablation removing contrastive/adversarial losses has mixed HRV/error outcomes (Table7), so no uniform component win.
utility_expert_privacy: No clinician or privacy study. Synthesis uses paired translation, not independent random sampling. RR results include many nearly zero SD values suggesting errors in peak timing or reporting.
reproducibility: Full arXiv v1 (52 pages), objective equations and code references; protocol has small selected test sets and epoch budgets differ among baselines.
critical_notes: Useful stress test for frequency adversarial losses, but HRV and paired RMSE should be reported alongside clinically meaningful intervals; this is adjacent PPG translation.

title: Lightweight Multi-task CNN for ECG Diagnosis with GRU-Diffusion
task_model: GRU-Diffusion synthesizes minority ECG beats for augmentation; separate multitask classifier (pp.3–11).
data_protocol: MIT-BIH two-lead and PTB 12-lead; selected single channel resampled250Hz,512 samples; shuffled80/20 record/sample split, no patient separation stated. Five minority MIT-BIH classes receive900 samples each.
metrics: PCA feature FID, mean/SD DTW for random real–synthetic pairs, Welch PSD then KL; classification metrics assess augmentation. Metric extractor, normalization and pairing detail limited (pp.8–9).
training_losses: Diffusion noise prediction follows DDPM; exact loss equation is standard DDPM MSE (Sec2.4), no extra ECG term. Separate DFNet classifier combines two cross-entropies and L2 regularization lambda=1e-5, task weights alpha/beta unspecified (p.7).
ablation_results: Table2 average FID64.43→16.13; mean DTW133.28→111, KL.044→.0226. Some per-class DTW worsens (VFW 220.96→141.68 still improvement; compare all class values). Table5 augmentation gains classifier scores but shuffled split risks record leakage.
utility_expert_privacy: Augmentation benefit is tested; no real/fake panel, physiological biomarker, privacy attack or held-out patient design reported.
reproducibility: PyTorch/RTR3090/Adam settings detailed; GAN/diffusion comparisons, loss schedule and exact feature model incomplete.
critical_notes: FID+DTW+PSD cover distinct domains, but PCA FID and random-pair DTW are implementation-sensitive. Classification lift under non-patient split may overstate utility.

title: A Physics-Aware Diffusion Framework for Robust ECG Synthesis Using Mesoscopic Lattice Boltzmann Constraints
task_model: PhysDiff-LBM diffusion reconstructs ECG from paired PPG using lattice-Boltzmann-inspired latent physics and QRS topology mask; included as generated-waveform translation subgroup.
data_protocol: MIMIC-III curated5000+ subjects and external VitalDB; PPG→ECG reconstruction; 128Hz, nonoverlap4s, min-max[-1,1], NeuroKit2/Pan-Tompkins (full text §§3.1–3.2). Exact split sizes and subject disjointness unclear.
metrics: Paired RMSE, Pan-Tompkins HR-MAE, raw-signal vector Fréchet distance; downstream AF/arrhythmia diagnostic metrics, t-SNE (evaluation §§3.2,3.5). Distribution FD treats flattened raw windows, not learned ECG features.
training_losses: Total lambda_diff noise-prediction MSE + lambda_reg QRS-mask BCE + lambda_phys squared temporal derivative versus LBM momentum field (Eqs.17–19); weights not specified. Preprocess uses128Hz/4s windows and 32-sample QRS mask (Eq.21).
ablation_results: Ablation table: full MIMIC RMSE .22, HRMAE1.26, FD6.23; VitalDB .25,1.95,4.35. No CIs/seeds in displayed table.
utility_expert_privacy: Paper claims downstream validity; independent classifier split and training/testing provenance require scrutiny. No clinicians or privacy attacks.
reproducibility: Full XML read; paper has equations/ablation, but high-level architecture and derived “clinical-grade” wording should not substitute for patient-level external validation.
critical_notes: Task is PPG-conditioned reconstruction, not free unconditional generation. Physical residual is against a fitted simplified model; agreement can reflect model assumptions.

title: Synthetic electrocardiograms for Brugada syndrome: from data generation to expert cardiologists evaluation
task_model: Pulse2Pulse GAN generates 12-lead Brugada-pattern ECGs and expert panel tests real/fake distinguishability (Methods/results).
data_protocol: 21 Brugada patients; 5-min 1kHz 12-lead real records, synthetic matched format; 1,122 generated segments? The evaluated set comprises 2244 ECG instances, half/half; same patient cohort as 2026 Zanchi validation.
metrics: Real/fake accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, F1; Cohen kappa within-rater between rounds; Wilcoxon round comparison (Statistical analysis section).
training_losses: GAN Pulse2Pulse details and objective delegated to prior paper, no coefficients/architecture/training split in article.
ablation_results: 7 Brugada specialists (>15y), blind, randomized2244 balanced traces, repeated after ≥2h. Accuracy40% then42%; sensitivity58%, specificity22→26%; kappa−.12 to.80 (Methods/results).
utility_expert_privacy: Strong expert-design detail, but same21-patient source and synthetic set as Zanchi2026; not independent replication. No held-out clinical outcome or privacy test.
reproducibility: Published full XML read; data governance/consent noted. Model full methods not reported, cite predecessor separately if needed.
critical_notes: Chance-level distinction supports perceptual similarity only, not clinical interchangeability; low specificity shows inconsistent labeling.

title: Reconstructing 12-lead ECG from 3-lead ECG using variational autoencoder to improve cardiac disease detection of wearable ECG devices
task_model: WearECG VAE reconstructs missing 12 leads from selected observed leads and evaluates reconstruction and physician reading; adjacent lead-translation included because it explicitly scores waveform generation.
data_protocol: MIMIC 12-lead records;500Hz Fourier resampling, patient_id grouped split; main input leads II,V1,V5, compare I/II/V3 and single I. Exact record counts/signal length not in inspected sections.
metrics: Paired MAE/MSE by lead; ECGFounder feature FID; 3 board-certified cardiologists blind Turing set50 mixed signals (52%,44%,44% correct); MI diagnosis on generated traces,55 cases: sensitivity100%,specificity44.8%,accuracy70.9%,F1 .765 (Results).
training_losses: VAE ELBO Eq.8, MSE reconstruction + beta KL(q(z|x)||N(0,I)), beta=1e-4; latent channels4, AdamW,10epochs (Methods).
ablation_results: Main leads II,V1,V5 overall MSE.00100, MAE.01782,FID12.64. Turing and MI confusion matrix as above.
utility_expert_privacy: Three experts assess realism and disease findings; MI assessment generated-only, specificity low; no utility vs paired real ECG or privacy attack.
reproducibility: Published XML and PDF; subject split explicit; supplements/checkpoints not inspected.
critical_notes: Reconstruction from partial observed leads relies on patient-specific paired signal, not population-level synthesis; near-chance detection does not validate safe diagnosis.

title: DiffECG: A Versatile Probabilistic Diffusion Model for ECG Signals Synthesis
task_model: Conditional DDPM with a task-aware U-Net for heartbeat generation, partial-signal imputation and forecasting; SERA 2024 publication qualifies although arXiv first report in 2023 is outside window.
data_protocol: MIT-BIH 48 records/two leads, 360Hz; MLII; annotated N,V,F beats of 270 samples around R peak; random 70/30 signal-wise split, not patient grouped (pp.3–4).
metrics: Generation RMSE/MAE, FID, DTW, EMD, MMD per class (Table II); downstream classifier accuracy/precision/recall/F1 after synthetic augmentation (Table I). Feature extractor details for FID are incomplete (pp.4–5).
training_losses: Conditional DDPM noise-prediction MSE Eq.3. Generation task masks all waveform values and conditions on class/task embeddings. Additional waveform MSE Eq.4 applies to imputation/forecasting, not unconditional generation (p.3).
ablation_results: Table II normal class: RMSE1.68e-3, DTW22.10, FID1.29e-2, EMD1.54e-2, MMD.40. One classifier F1 rises .77→.96 with synthetic augmentation (Table I). Other class metrics are mixed versus strongest GAN baselines.
utility_expert_privacy: Three classifier baselines evaluated with real-only and synthetic augmentation. No experts/privacy attack. Signal-wise split risks patient leakage; no external data.
reproducibility: Full arXiv PDF;1000 diffusion steps, beta .0001–.02, Adam .001. No run intervals. IEEE SERA DOI10.1109/SERA61261.2024.10685651, conference date 2024-05-30.
critical_notes: Unified task-aware architecture is useful, but metric implementation is incomplete and record-level splitting may inflate evaluation. Restrict conclusions to reported protocol.
